context: Builds on saving NFS export options and testing approved client access. Here an existing old mount affects when you can publish the saved policy in the simulator.
goal: Remove an obsolete share from the server’s current export list while preserving the archive mount and approved reference access.

concepts.title: Read the current export list
concepts.text: The virtual /etc/exports file holds saved settings. Saving an edit does not publish it. On the server, exportfs -v reports which paths and access options are applied now.

concepts.title: Re-export after checking current mounts
concepts.text: Use exportfs -r or exportfs -ra to publish the saved settings in this exercise. This simulator refuses to change an export when a conflicting current mount depends on it. Unmount only the retired client. Preserve independent working shares.

concepts.title: Verify the client experience
concepts.text: showmount -e with the server address shows what the supplied NFSv3 server advertises. A client must still mount the right path and have permission to read its file. Try a fresh mount for the retired client as well.

worked.label: Compare saved and applied
worked.explanation: The old /srv/demo-drop export is still visible while the current rules remain applied.

worked.label: Resolve a conflicting mount
worked.explanation: Remove only the demo-drop rule and select Save export file. Select Unmount retired client, then run the command. Leave the archive mount in place.

worked.label: Verify the current list and actual access
worked.explanation: The old path is absent. Select Mount approved share and Read reference file to verify that approved access still works.

practice.title: Save one retirement
practice.action: Check the draft in Server file. Remove only the line for /srv/demo-drop and select Save export file.
practice.observe: The display marks your changes saved. The current server still uses its earlier export list.

practice.title: Compare and try to re-export
practice.action: Run exportfs -v and showmount -e 192.0.2.10. Try exportfs -ra while the old client mount is still present.
practice.observe: The old path remains visible and the simulator refuses the conflicting re-export. Your saved changes stay in place.

practice.title: Remove the old mount and verify
practice.action: Select Unmount retired client, then run exportfs -ra and repeat showmount -e. Select Test retired mount, Mount approved share, and Read reference file. Finish with Check workspace.
practice.observe: The retired client receives no mount. The approved client can read the file and the archive mount is preserved.

requirements: Save a revised export file that removes the old-bundle share. Keep both remaining export rules unchanged and re-export without disturbing the archive mount.
Confirm a fresh retired client cannot mount the old share. The approved client should mount the reference share and read its supplied file.
Keep the contents of all the existing files intact.

review.introduction: Distinguishes saved file, applied server output, advertised share and actual client access before practice.
review.example: Checks one intended virtual retirement and the simulator’s active-mount refusal with typed commands and a separate known source.
review.assignment: Keeps independent meaningful configuration, mount, file-preservation and denied fresh request checks in an isolated typed workspace.
